newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Energy delays Pt Beach 2 restart.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Energy delays Pt Beach 2 restart.

text.p: Wisconsin Electric, a subsidiary of Wisconsin Energy Co, said Thursday it was delaying restart of its Point Beach 2 nuclear power plant.

The delay was pompted by mechanical problems at the 485 megawatt (MW) unit. The company had planned to return the unit to service later this week following a refueling outage that started in October, 1996.
"A seal in a reactor coolant pump has failed to seat properly at Wisconsin Electric's Point Beach Nuclear Plant," the company said in a statement.
"Removal of the pump motor and replacement of the seal will postpone restart of...Unit 2 until mid-August."

The 485 MW Point Beach nuclear unit 1 is still expected to return to service two to three weeks after the restart of unit 2, Wisconsin Electric said. Point Beach 1 was shut in February for maintenance.
The company said it has asked power customers to continue energy conservation measures, especially during periods of hot and humid weather.
"The regional power supply remains tight with roughly 30 percent of the region's nuclear generation out of service and limited ability to buy and transport power into the state," the company said.
The power supply situation would be aided by the beginning of operations at the 230 MW LS Power cogeneration plant being constructed at Whitewater, Wisc., the company said.
The new plant was to have begun operations June 1, but remains out of service with expected commercial operation by early August and possible limted availability next week, Wisconsin Electric said.
Wisconsin Electric provides power to about 2.3 million people in southeastern Wisconsin, the Appleton area, the Prairie du Chien area, and in northeastern Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula.
